Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

State Bank of India (SBI) has provided a marks download facility for Circle Based Officer (CBO) recruitment, under Advt. No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18, alongside the Final Result declared on 24 July 2026. This page explains how to download your SBI CBO marks, how the written exam and interview marks are calculated into the final merit score, and what is known so far about cut-off marks.

SBI CBO Marks 2026 - Quick Overview

Particular Details
Organization State Bank of India (SBI)
Post Name Circle Based Officer (CBO)
Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18
Marks Available For Objective Test, Descriptive Test, Interview
Online Exam Held On 14 March 2026
Interview Conducted From 13 July 2026 onward
Marks Download Link Provided Yes, on official careers portal
Login Required Roll Number/Registration Number and Date of Birth (as per standard SBI process; confirm on portal)
Official Website sbi.bank.in/web/careers

SBI CBO Exam Pattern: Marks Breakup

Test Marks Duration Notes
Objective Test 120 - No negative marking; no sectional qualifying marks
Descriptive Test (Letter Writing & Essay) 50 30 minutes Two questions; typed/online mode
Total Online Test 170 - Objective + Descriptive combined
Interview 50 - Minimum qualifying marks apply as decided by the Bank

SBI CBO Final Merit Score: How Marks Are Combined

  • Online Test score (out of 170) is converted to a weightage of 75
  • Interview score (out of 50) is converted to a weightage of 25
  • Final merit score is out of 100, prepared Circle-wise and Category-wise

Formula (as applied in this recruitment pattern):

Final Score = (Online Test Marks ÷ 170 × 75) + (Interview Marks ÷ 50 × 25)

How to Download SBI CBO Marks 2026

  1. Visit the official SBI careers portal: sbi.bank.in/web/careers.
  2. Go to "Current Openings" and find the Circle Based Officer recruitment link under Advt. No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18.
  3. Click the "Download Marks" or "Scorecard" link.
  4. Log in using your Roll Number/Registration Number and Date of Birth, if prompted.
  5. View and download your section-wise/stage-wise marks.
  6. Save a copy for your records before the link is taken down.

Documents to Keep Ready After Checking Marks

  • Printed scorecard/marks PDF
  • Roll Number and Registration Number
  • Interview call letter (if applicable)
  • Original and photocopies of educational certificates and mark sheets
  • Valid government photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, or Driving Licence)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), where applicable
  • Recent passport-size photographs

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has released the PNB LBO Score Card 2026 for candidates who appeared in the Local Bank Officer (LBO) online written examination held on 4 January 2026. The individual scorecard link went live on the official recruitment page on 1 August 2026 and can be accessed through a registration-based login on the ibpsreg.ibps.in portal. This article explains how to download your scorecard, what it contains, the qualifying marks, and the last date to access it.

Direct Link to Check PNB LBO Score Card 2026

PNB LBO Score Card 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Organization Punjab National Bank (PNB)
Post Name Local Bank Officer (LBO), Scale I / JMGS-I
Recruitment Notification Date 3 November 2025
Online Written Exam Date 4 January 2026
Written Exam Result / LLPT-Interview Call Letter 24 April 2026
Final Result Declared 23 June 2026
Scorecard Release Date 1 August 2026
Scorecard Portal ibpsreg.ibps.in
Login Credentials Required Registration/Application Number + Password or Date of Birth
Official Website pnb.bank.in

PNB LBO Score Card 2026: Important Dates

Event Date
Recruitment Notification Published 3 November 2025
Online Written Examination 4 January 2026
Notice for Language Test and Interview / Written Result Update 24 April 2026
Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) 2 May 2026
Personal Interview 3 to 5 May 2026
Final Result Declared 23 June 2026
Joining Schedule (First Batch) 30 June 2026
Joining Schedule – Second and Final Opportunity 29 July 2026
Individual Scorecard Link Activated 1 August 2026, 4:15 PM
Scorecard Download Window Closes 31 August 2026, 11:55 PM

What the PNB LBO Score Card 2026 Contains

The individual scorecard is a diagnostic document distinct from the result PDF. It is issued to candidates who appeared in the online written test, regardless of whether they ultimately qualified. It typically displays:

  • Candidate's roll number and registration number
  • Section-wise marks scored in the online written examination
  • Overall/aggregate marks
  • Qualifying status (Qualified / Not Qualified) for that stage

Also Read: UP TGT 2026 Special Document Verification Admit Card

How to Download PNB LBO Score Card 2026

  1. Visit the official PNB recruitment page at pnb.bank.in, or go directly to the ibpsreg.ibps.in scorecard login portal.
  2. Locate the notice titled "Link to View Individual Scorecard" under the Local Bank Officer recruitment section.
  3. Enter your Registration Number / Application Number in the first field.
  4. Enter your Password, or your Date of Birth in DD-MM-YYYY format, in the second field.
  5. Click the Login/Submit button.
  6. Your section-wise scorecard will be displayed on screen.
  7. Download the PDF, or use Ctrl+P to save it as a PDF if no direct download option is shown.
  8. Take a printout and store it safely you will need it during document verification and joining formalities.

PNB LBO Written Exam Qualifying Marks (Cut Off)

As reported by exam-preparation portals covering this recruitment cycle, candidates were required to clear both an overall cut off and a minimum sectional cut off in the online written test:

Category Minimum Marks Required Per Section
General / EWS 40%
SC / ST / OBC / PwBD 35%

Note: These sectional cut off percentages are drawn from exam-reporting sources and are consistent with the standard IBPS-pattern cut off structure used in this recruitment; they are Not Available Officially as an explicitly stated figure on PNB's own notice text reviewed for this article. Candidates should cross-check exact figures against their own scorecard.

Separately, some exam-prep sources report an interview qualifying score of 25 out of 50 for General category candidates and 22.5 out of 50 for SC/ST candidates. This detail is Not Available Officially on PNB's recruitment notice board and should be treated as unconfirmed until verified against the official result document.

Documents Required at the Time of Document Verification / Joining

  • Printed copy of the PNB LBO Score Card 2026
  • Final Result / Provisional Selection intimation
  • Valid photo ID proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, Driving License, etc.)
  • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • Proof of post-qualification banking experience (as applicable to the LBO eligibility criteria)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD), if applicable
  • Recent passport-size photographs

Also Read: UPSSSC VDO Supplementary Result 2026

Important Instructions

  • The scorecard link is active only for a limited window (1 August to 31 August 2026). Download it before the window closes.
  • Use your registration number rather than your name to search for your record, since candidate names can repeat.
  • Report any discrepancy in personal details on the scorecard to PNB/IBPS immediately rather than proceeding with an incorrect document.
  • PNB has issued a public notice warning candidates against paying any money to anyone for interview calls, selection, or appointment. The bank does not charge any fee for these purposes.
  • Keep your scorecard along with your final result document for document verification and joining formalities.

Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Result 2026: Punjab and Sind Bank has declared the result for the Apprentice Recruitment 2026 on 30 July 2026. The recruitment drive was conducted for a total of 635 Apprentice vacancies across various states and union territories in India. Candidates who applied online between 21 May 2026 and 6 June 2026 can now download the merit list PDF and check whether their name or roll number is included in the shortlist. Selection has been made purely on the basis of merit prepared from HSC/10+2 marks, followed by document verification. The direct download link for the Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Result 2026 PDF is available in the Important Links section below.

Candidates are advised to download the official merit list PDF and carefully verify their name, roll number, and allotted state/district before proceeding to the next stage of document verification.

How to Check Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Result 2026

  1. Visit the official website of Punjab and Sind Bank at punjabandsind.bank.in, or use the direct result PDF link given in the Important Links table below.
  2. Look for the link titled "Apprentice Result 2026" or "Apprentice Merit List 2026" under the Careers/Recruitment section.
  3. Click on the link to open the Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Result 2026 PDF.
  4. Use Ctrl+F (or the search option in your PDF viewer) to search for your name, roll number, or registration number.
  5. Download and save the PDF, or take a screenshot of the page showing your details for future reference.

Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Selection Process 2026

The Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026 selection process does not include any written examination. Selection has been made entirely on the following basis:

  • Merit list prepared from HSC/10+2 marks of applicants
  • Merit list drawn state-wise, district-wise, and category-wise
  • In case of a tie in marks, older candidates are given preference in ranking
  • Document verification of shortlisted candidates
  • Medical fitness verification as per the bank's requirements

Documents Required at the Document Verification Stage

  • Valid original photo ID proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, etc.)

  • Class 12 (HSC/10+2) mark sheet and certificate
  • Graduation degree/provisional certificate and mark sheets
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD), if applicable
  • Recent passport-size photographs
  • Any other document specifically mentioned in the official result notice or call letter

Punjab and Sind Bank Apprentice Important Instructions

  • Download the merit list PDF only from the official Punjab and Sind Bank website or the verified links shared in this article.
  • Selected candidates will not be treated as regular employees of the bank and will not be entitled to employee benefits during the apprenticeship period.
  • No daily allowance, conveyance allowance, or travelling allowance is payable to apprentices apart from the fixed monthly stipend.
  • The apprenticeship does not guarantee any offer of permanent employment after completion of the 12-month training period.
  • Keep a printed copy and a digital copy of the result/merit list PDF safe for all future reference and communication with the bank.
  • Regularly check the official website and registered email/SMS for updates on document verification and joining formalities.

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) has released the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 on 31st July 2026 for candidates who appeared in the CRP RRBs-XIV recruitment cycle. This is the 1st Reserve List, and it gives another chance to candidates who cleared the exam but were not allotted a bank in the main result. Candidates can log in to the official IBPS portal with their registration/roll number and password/date of birth to check their provisional allotment status.

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026: Vacancy Details

Why Was the Reserve List Released?

After the CRP RRBs-XIV final result, a primary list of selected candidates was allotted to participating rural banks. However, some sanctioned posts remained vacant because certain selected candidates did not join within the deadline, resigned soon after joining, or were excluded during document verification. To ensure these vacancies are filled, IBPS has released this reserve list for candidates who cleared the exam but were not allotted a bank in the first round.

How to Check IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026

  1. Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
  2. Click on the "IBPS RRB CRP-CSA (Customer Service Associate)" link on the homepage.

  4. Enter your Registration No/Roll No and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Enter the captcha code and click Login.
  6. Check your provisional allotment status and download it for future reference.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Candidates provisionally allotted from the reserve list will also receive an intimation email and SMS on their registered contact details.
  • The allotment shown after login is provisional and will be confirmed only after the concerned bank completes document and eligibility verification.
  • Specific documents required for verification are not listed in the official notification. Candidates should follow the instructions issued directly by their allotted bank.
  • Candidates should keep checking their registered email and SMS regularly to avoid missing further communication or deadlines.

What Happens After Reserve List Allotment?

Based on the notification, candidates allotted through the reserve list can expect the following process, though exact dates and requirements are not specified:

  • Document Verification
  • Submission of Required Certificates
  • Medical Examination (if applicable)
  • Joining Formalities
  • Induction/Training Process

Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) released the IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026 on 29th July 2026 for candidates appearing in the recruitment exam for 750 Apprentice posts. The online examination is scheduled for 2nd August 2026. The admit card carries the candidate's roll number, exam centre details, reporting time, and exam-day instructions. Candidates who applied for the IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026 must download and carry a printed copy of the call letter to the exam, as it is mandatory for entry.

How to Download IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026?

Candidates can download their IOB Apprentice Call Letter 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Open the registered email ID that was used during the application process.
  2. Look for the email sent by BFSI SSC containing the IOB Apprentice Call Letter 2026.
  3. Open the email and click on the admit card download link, or download the attached PDF if provided.
  4. Check every detail on the admit card, including your name, roll number, exam date, reporting time, and exam-day instructions.
  5. Download and save the admit card on your device.
  6. Take at least two clear printouts of the hall ticket and carry one along with a valid photo ID on exam day.

Details Mentioned on the IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Candidates should verify each of the following details carefully upon downloading their call letter:

  • Candidate's Full Name & Roll Number
  • Registration Number & Post Discipline (Apprentice)
  • Exam Date, Shift Timing & Reporting Time
  • Complete Name & Address of Exam Centre (or remote exam instructions, as applicable)
  • Candidate's Photograph & Digital Signature
  • Category & Gender
  • Exam Day Rules & Code of Conduct

IOB Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

The online examination consists of 100 objective-type questions carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 90 minutes, across four sections:

Section No. of Questions Maximum Marks
General / Financial Awareness 25 25
General English 25 25
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 25 25
Computer or Subject Knowledge 25 25
Total 100 100

Total exam duration: 90 minutes.

IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026: Important Instructions

  • Carry a clear printed copy of the IOB Apprentice Call Letter along with an original photo ID such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Passport, or Driving Licence.
  • Check the reporting time mentioned on your admit card and reach the reporting location (exam centre, or your home setup if the exam is confirmed as remote-proctored) well ahead of the scheduled time.
  • Do not carry mobile phones, smartwatches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, or any study material into the examination hall, if attending at a physical centre.
  • Ensure your photograph, signature, and other personal details on the admit card are clearly visible before exam day.
  • If the exam is remote-proctored, ensure a working device with a front camera, microphone, and stable internet connection, as per the instructions on your specific call letter.

What to Do in Case of an Issue in the IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026?

If any discrepancy is found on the admit card, candidates should act promptly:

  1. Verify the name, date of birth, and category details carefully.
  2. Check whether the photograph and signature are clearly visible.
  3. Confirm the exam date, time, and exam centre/mode details.
  4. Contact the helpdesk through the official support channels on iob.in or the BFSI SSC portal if any information is incorrect.
  5. Keep the application form and registration details ready while requesting corrections.
  6. Download the corrected IOB Apprentice Admit Card PDF once the issue is resolved.

Union Bank of India has released the result for engagement of apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961. Candidates who appeared for the online written test conducted by BFSI SSC on 07.06.2026 can now check their roll number in the state-wise provisional selection list. The result was declared by the Human Resources Vertical, Central Office, Mumbai on 24.07.2026.

Union Bank of India Apprentice Result 2026: Direct PDF Download Link

Union Bank of India has announced the Apprentice Result 2026 for the recruitment conducted under the Apprentices Act, 1961. Candidates who appeared for the online written examination held on 07 June 2026 can use the direct link below to download the official result PDF and check their roll number in the state-wise provisional selection list.

Click Here to Download Union Bank of India Apprentice Result 2026 PDF

Union Bank of India Apprentice Result 2026: How to Check Your Roll Number

The result has been released as a state-wise PDF containing roll numbers of provisionally selected candidates. To check your name in the list:

  1. Open the official result PDF using the link given in the Important Links table below.
  2. Use Ctrl+F (or Command+F on Mac) to search the page.
  3. Locate your state name, then type your roll number to find it in the list.
  4. Save or take a screenshot of the page for future reference.

The roll numbers are grouped state-wise, covering candidates across Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Odisha, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal.

Also Read: SBI CBO Final Result 2026 Out - Download PDF, Check Selected Candidates List

Union Bank of India Apprentice Selection Process

As per the result notice, final selection depends on successful completion of the following activities after the provisional result:

  1. Fulfilment of eligibility criteria/conditions as prescribed in the notification dated 28.04.2026, verified during Document Verification.
  2. Language Proficiency Test (for applicable candidates).
  3. Submission of Medical Fitness Certificate as mentioned in the notification dated 28.04.2026.

The Bank has clearly stated that selection is provisional and subject to production of all relevant documentary evidence supporting eligibility at the time of reporting.

Documents Required for Union Bank of India Apprentice Document Verification

Selected candidates must carry the following documents at the time of reporting:

  • 10 photographs (as uploaded on the NATS Portal)
  • Address Proof (Permanent and Communication)
  • PAN Card / Proof of PAN allotment
  • Aadhaar Card
  • All original certificates supporting eligibility (10th/Matriculation, 12th onwards) — both Degree and Marksheet must be produced
  • Caste Certificate (for SC/ST/OBC candidates) and Permanent PwBD Certificate (for candidates under the Disabled Category); OBC Certificate must carry the "Non-Creamy Layer" clause
  • EWS Certificate valid for FY 2025-26, if applicable
  • One self-attested photocopy set of all documents/certificates/IDs
  • Medical Fitness Certificate from a practicing registered general physician (minimum MBBS qualification)
  • Printout of the NATS Portal profile

Union Bank of India Apprentice Important Instructions

  • This result notice is treated as intimation to all candidates who appeared in the selection process; no separate communication will be sent to non-selected candidates.
  • A detailed communication with the venue and reporting date for document verification will be sent only to the registered email ID of selected candidates.
  • The Bank has stated that all care has been taken in compiling the result, but it reserves the right to rectify any error.
  • The Bank's decision on all matters relating to the selection process is final and binding.

The State Bank of India (SBI) has declared the SBI Circle Based Officer (CBO) Final Result 2026 on 24 July 2026 for Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18, dated 29 January 2026. The result lists the roll numbers of candidates provisionally selected for the CBO post following interviews held in July 2026. Candidates can download the official PDF from sbi.bank.in and check their roll number in the list below.

Reader advisory: This article covers only Advt No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18 (the January 2026 CBO drive, exam held 14 March 2026). SBI has separately run an earlier CBO recruitment under Advt No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/03, whose final result was declared in November 2025 with 2,964 vacancies - that is a different recruitment cycle. Please confirm which advertisement number applies to your application before checking your result.

SBI CBO Final Result 2026: Direct PDF Download Link

The State Bank of India (SBI) has released the Circle Based Officer (CBO) Final Result 2026 for Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18 on its official careers portal. Candidates who appeared for the interview can use the direct link below to download the official result PDF and check their roll number in the list of provisionally selected candidates.

Click Here to Download SBI CBO Final Result 2026 PDF

SBI CBO Final Result 2026: What the PDF Says

The official final result notice, signed by the General Manager, states that the listed roll numbers belong to candidates provisionally selected as Circle Based Officers. The selection is explicitly subject to two conditions mentioned in the PDF:

  • Qualifying the Proficiency Test in Local Language(s)
  • Fulfilment of eligibility criteria and conditions as prescribed in Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18 dated 29.01.2026

This means candidates whose roll numbers appear in the list have not yet received a final, unconditional offer - the Local Language Proficiency Test and document/eligibility verification are still pending. The official PDF does not state the total number of candidates selected; this figure is Not Available Officially at this time.

How to Download SBI CBO Final Result 2026 PDF

  1. Visit the official SBI careers portal at sbi.bank.in.
  2. Go to the "Careers" section and click "Current Openings."
  3. Look for "Recruitment of Circle Based Officer" against Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18.
  4. Click the final result / list of provisionally selected candidates link.
  5. Use Ctrl+F (on desktop) to search your roll number or registration number in the PDF.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

Also Read: UPSC ESE Mains Result 2026 Out - Download Engineering Services Main Exam Written Result PDF

What Happens After the SBI CBO Final Result?

Provisionally selected candidates should watch for further communication from SBI regarding:

  • Local Language Proficiency Test schedule (Not Yet Announced)
  • Document verification / biodata form submission
  • Joining formalities and posting circle confirmation

Selected candidates will be posted in the Circle of the State against which they applied and selected, and will not be entitled to an inter-circle transfer until promotion to SMGS-IV grade or completion of 12 years of service, whichever is later - as per the terms of the original advertisement.

Important Instructions

  • The result is provisional; it does not guarantee final appointment.
  • Candidates must retain a downloaded copy of the result PDF for future reference.
  • Any discrepancy in personal or roll number details should be reported to SBI through official channels only.
  • Candidates are advised to rely only on sbi.bank.in for official updates and to treat vacancy or date figures from third-party sites as indicative unless confirmed against the official PDF.

IOB Chief Financial Officer Eligibility Criteria 2026

All eligibility criteria (Qualification, Age, Experience, etc.) for this post shall be computed as on 01.07.2026 (inclusive).

Educational/Professional Qualification

  • A qualified Chartered Accountant
  • Preferred: FRM Certification and/or CFA

Work Experience

Minimum fifteen (15) years in overseeing financial operations, preferably accounting and taxation matters, in Banks/large corporates/PSUs/FIs/financial services organizations, of which ten (10) years should be in Banks/FIs, of which five (5) years should be at Senior Management level.

Age Limit

Maximum age 55 years (inclusive of applicable age relaxation), as on 01.07.2026.

Nationality/Citizenship

A candidate must be either:

  • a Citizen of India, or
  • a subject of Nepal, or
  • a subject of Bhutan, or
  • a Tibetan refugee who came over to India before 1st January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or
  • a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, East African countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania (formerly Tanganyika and Zanzibar), Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia and Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.

Candidates belonging to categories (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v) above must possess a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India before the date of this notification.

IOB Chief Financial Officer: Roles & Responsibilities

  • Financial Reporting & Compliance: Overseeing the statutory auditing process, reporting audit results as per SEBI requirements, monitoring critical financial parameters (Non-Interest Income, ROA, ROE etc.), coordinating with NFRA and RBI on auditor-related issues, and handling Whole Bank Long Form Audit Report (WBLFAR) matters.
  • Tax Compliance: Optimization of the Bank's tax liability, GST and TDS compliance.
  • Accounting Systems: Developing and maintaining accounting systems per Accounting Standards and RBI Guidelines, Internal Financial Controls over Financial Reporting (IFCOFR), and implementation of IFRS/IND AS.
  • Management Reporting: Coordinating with the Financial Control Department for review of regional and Whole Bank performance.
  • International Banking Activities: Supporting the International Banking Group on accounting and tax compliance as per local regulators.
  • Other Activities: Overseeing MIS reporting systems, strategic capital planning, balance sheet optimization, medium-term financial strategy, and managing stakeholder relationships with regulators, government, rating agencies, and investors.

IOB Chief Financial Officer Selection Process 2026

  • Selection will be through Personal Interview/Discussion. The Bank may carry out a preliminary screening of applications to shortlist eligible candidates based on qualifications, suitability, and experience.
  • Total marks allocated for the Personal Interview: 100.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 50 (45 for OBC/SC/ST/PwBD candidates).
  • In case multiple candidates score the same cut-off marks, ranking will be done according to age, in descending order.
  • The Bank may change the mode of selection depending on the number of applications received.
  • Merely fulfilling the minimum qualification and experience criteria does not automatically entitle a candidate to an interview call; the Bank may consider additional qualifications, greater experience, and level of responsibilities handled while shortlisting.

IOB Chief Financial Officer: Joining, Bond & Probation

  • The selected candidate, at the time of joining, must execute a Bond of Rs. 3 lakhs to serve the Bank for a stipulated period of 3 years. The Bond will be invoked if the candidate resigns before the expiry of the bond period from the date of joining.
  • On joining, the selected candidate will be on probation for a period of 1 year and subjected to continuous assessment. Confirmation depends on qualifying the assessment as per standards determined by the Bank.
  • If the candidate fails to achieve the minimum stipulated standards, their services may be terminated.
  • Place of Posting: Central Office, Chennai.

  • Valid system-generated printout of the registered online application form

The land loser and/or their spouse, son, daughter, grandson, or granddaughter are eligible under the landloser quota.
  • Employment Exchange Registered Candidates: Domiciles of Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka with valid employment exchange cards registered along the Konkan Railway route (Raigad, Sindhudurg, and Ratnagiri districts of Maharashtra; Goa State; Uttara Kannada, Udupi, and Dakshina Kannada/South Kannada districts of Karnataka).
  • Other Domicile Candidates: Candidates domiciled in the States of Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka (not covered above).
  • KRCL Employees: Serving KRCL employees who have completed at least 3 years of regular service.

Note: Recruitment in the erstwhile Group-D post - Track Maintainer - is limited to eligible Land Loser candidates only.

Preference in Recruitment

Candidates securing the minimum qualifying marks are given preference for recruitment in the following order:

  1. Land Loser candidates (first preference)
  2. Candidates registered in Employment Exchanges along the KR route (second preference)
  3. Candidates domiciled in Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka, and KRCL employees (third preference)

Candidates must declare their status (Land Loser/Employment Exchange/Domicile) at the time of application; this choice is final. The second and third panels are operated only after exhausting the panel of eligible land losers.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details

KRCL has announced 201 vacancies across 12 posts. Category-wise reservation (UR/EWS/OBC-NCL/SC/ST) is shown in parentheses against each post; the notification also provides horizontal reservation for Ex-Servicemen (Ex.SM) and PwBD within these totals.

The age of candidates shall be reckoned as on 01/08/2026.

Candidates eligible for relaxation on more than one ground get the benefit of the category with maximum relaxation only - not cumulative.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Reservation Policy

This notification provides Vertical Reservation for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, and EWS, and Horizontal Reservation for Ex-Servicemen (Ex.SM) and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD).

  • EWS Reservation: Candidates not covered under SC/ST/OBC-NCL reservation, whose family gross annual income is below Rs. 8 lakh and who do not own specified categories of land/property, can claim EWS reservation with a valid Income & Asset Certificate.
  • Note: EBC and EWS are different categories - EBC candidates get fee concession only, not job reservation.
  • Horizontal Reservation: Ex-Servicemen and PwBD reservations are included within the post-wise vacancies shown above, irrespective of social community. Ex.SM and PwBD candidates can also apply against unreserved vacancies of posts not exclusively earmarked for them (PwBD candidates only where the post is indicated as suitable for their disability), and are eligible for age relaxation and fee exemption.
  • PwBD Categories: VI (Visually Impaired: Blind/Low Vision), HI (Hearing Impaired: Deaf/Hard of Hearing), LD (Locomotor Disability: One Arm/One Leg/One Arm-Leg/Dwarfism) - subject to a minimum of 40% disability. One Commercial Supervisor post is reserved for PwBD candidates.
  • EWS, SC, ST, and OBC-NCL candidates who qualify without relaxed standards will not be adjusted against reserved vacancies and will be considered under UR.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Exam Pattern (CBT)

The recruitment process varies by post group:

  • Section Controller, Station Master, Assistant Loco Pilot: CBT → Computer-Based/OMR-based Aptitude Test → Document Verification (DV) → Medical Examination. Merit is prepared with 70% weightage to CBT marks and 30% to Aptitude Test marks.
  • Senior Section Engineer (Mechanical/S&T), Junior Engineer (Civil/Mechanical), Goods Train Manager, Commercial Supervisor, Technician-III (Mechanical), ESTM-III: CBT → Document Verification → Medical Examination.
  • Track Maintainer: CBT → Document Verification → Physical Efficiency Test (PET) → Medical Examination.

The CBT is of screening nature with negative marking - one mark is deducted for each wrong answer. Questions are set in five languages: English, Hindi, Marathi, Konkani, and Kannada (the Aptitude Test for SCOR/SM/ALP is in English and Hindi only).

The full unit-wise technical syllabus for each post - covering subjects such as Engineering Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Building Materials & Construction, Surveying, Thermal Engineering, Basic Electricity/Electronics, and related topics - is detailed separately in the official notification (Section 14.7 to 14.14) and should be reviewed in full by candidates preparing for the CBT.

PET is mandatory and qualifying in nature, conducted in two stages - Weight Carrying first, followed by a Running Test. Failing the Weight Carrying stage results in elimination at that stage itself.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

Category Examination Fee
UR / OBC-NCL / General candidates Rs. 1,180/- (Rs. 1,000 + 18% GST) + payment gateway charges, per examination
SC / ST / Ex-Servicemen / Female / Minorities / EBC / PwBD Fee is refunded (minus bank charges) upon appearing in the CBT

Fee is payable online only, through Internet Banking, Debit/Credit Cards, or UPI. Minorities include Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, and Zoroastrians (Parsis). Economically Backward Class (EBC) candidates - annual family income below Rs. 50,000 - get fee concession only, not job reservation. There is no refund for erroneous, incomplete, or rejected applications.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Documents Required

Candidates should keep scanned copies of the following ready before filling the online application:

  • Recent colour passport-size photograph (JPEG, 30–70 KB, plain white background, no cap/dark glasses)
  • Scanned signature in running handwriting (JPEG, 30–70 KB)
  • SC/ST certificate (for candidates seeking free rail travel passes)
  • PwBD candidates: additional passport-size photograph as per specification, and Scribe details/photograph if applicable

At the time of Document Verification (DV), candidates must produce original documents along with self-attested photocopies, including:

  • Matriculation/High School Certificate (proof of Date of Birth and qualification)
  • HSC, Graduation, and ITI/NCVT-SCVT certificates as applicable
  • Aadhaar Card and PAN Card
  • Domicile certificate (Maharashtra/Goa/Karnataka)
  • SC/ST/OBC-NCL caste certificate in the prescribed Annexure format, where applicable
  • Income Certificate for EBC fee waiver / EWS Income & Asset Certificate, where applicable
  • PwBD certificate as per the prescribed Annexure, where applicable
  • NOC from current employer (for serving Govt./PSU employees) and discharge certificate (for Ex-Servicemen)
  • Land Loser candidates: SLAO Land Loser Certificate, Tehsildar's certificate, proof of relationship, and RTC land documents, as applicable

How to Apply for KRCL Recruitment 2026

Interested and eligible candidates can apply online for KRCL Recruitment 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Visit the official KRCL website, www.konkanrailway.com, once the application link goes live (tentatively last week of August 2026).
  2. Register your name on the portal; a Registration Number will be generated and sent via registered email and mobile number, along with a password and application link.
  3. Activate the link to access the application form and fill in personal, educational, and category details, carefully selecting your post-wise preference (this cannot be changed once submitted).
  4. Pay the prescribed examination fee online for each CBT Examination Group selected, using Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, or UPI.
  5. Upload the required scanned documents - photograph, signature, and category certificates (if applicable).
  6. Review all entries carefully, then submit the application before the closing date.
  7. Keep a printed copy of the submitted online application for future reference - do not send it to KRCL by post.

Candidates are advised to apply only through the official KRCL website and to be cautious of fake websites and job racketeers, as KRCL has not appointed any agents or coaching centres on its behalf.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for one or more posts in a single application, in order of preference; once exercised, post preference is final and cannot be changed.
  • KRCL will allot only one post to a selected candidate, based on preference, merit, vacancy position, and qualifying the selection stages - no request for a lower-preference post will be entertained after allotment.
  • Serving Government/PSU employees may apply directly but must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer at the time of DV, failing which their candidature will be cancelled.
  • Selected candidates can be posted anywhere within KRCL's area of operation, including project sites; KRCL employees are not eligible for transfer to other Zonal Railways.
  • Candidates must ensure their mobile number and email ID are active throughout the recruitment process, as all communication will be via SMS and email only.
  • Any candidate found using unfair means, impersonation, or furnishing false information will be disqualified and debarred from future KRCL examinations, and is liable for legal action.
  • KRCL reserves the right to change the number of vacancies, cancel the recruitment process in part or full, and reject applications without assigning reasons.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Important Links

  • Official Notification PDF: Click here
  • Official Website: Click here 

Land Loser candidates, Employment Exchange-registered candidates along the Konkan Railway route, domiciles of Maharashtra/Goa/Karnataka, and serving KRCL employees with 3+ years of regular service are eligible, subject to post-wise qualification and age criteria.

Candidates who have completed a Diploma or Degree in Engineering can also explore more Diploma Government Jobs and Engineering Government Jobs available across India. Candidates interested in railway sector opportunities can also check the latest Railway Recruitment 2026 notifications from RRB and other railway zones. Those looking for openings closer to the region can browse Maharashtra Government Jobs and Goa Government Jobs for upcoming vacancies. 10th and 12th pass candidates can also explore more ITI Government Jobs and Track Maintainer Jobs matching their qualification.

How to Download the RRB Ministerial & Isolated Categories Answer Key 2026?

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB region, or use the common portal link.
  2. Look for the notification link titled "CEN No. 08/2025 - Ministerial and Isolated Categories Answer Key 2026" under the Latest Updates or Answer Key/Objection section.
  3. Click the link, which will redirect to the login page.
  4. Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password in the login fields.
  5. Click "Login" to view your recorded responses, question paper, and the provisional answer key.
  6. Use the "Save/Print" option to download the answer key and response sheet as a PDF.

Candidates are advised to take a printout of both the answer key and their response sheet for offline review.

How to Calculate Marks Using the RRB MI Answer Key?

The RRB Ministerial & Isolated Categories CBT carries 100 marks for 100 questions. Use the following marking scheme to estimate your score:

  • Correct Answer: +1 mark
  • Incorrect Answer: -1/3 (0.33) mark deducted
  • Unattempted Question: 0 marks

Formula: Total Marks = (Number of Correct Answers × 1) - (Number of Wrong Answers × 0.33)

How to Raise Objections Against the RRB MI Answer Key 2026?

  1. Log in to the official answer key portal using your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password.
  2. Locate the "Raise Objection" or "Challenge Answer Key" option on your dashboard.
  3. Select the specific question ID and the answer option you believe is incorrect.
  4. Upload a valid justification or supporting reference (textbook page, authoritative source, etc.) for each challenged question. Objections without proof are not considered.
  5. Pay the objection fee of Rs. 50 per question (plus applicable bank charges) via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or Net Banking.
  6. Submit the form and save the confirmation/acknowledgement for future reference.

Objection Window 31 July 2026 (11:55 PM) to 7 August 2026 (11:55 PM)
Payment Modes Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, Net Banking

Objections submitted after the closing date, or through email/post, will not be entertained.

Important Instructions

  • Only the provisional answer key is currently available; scores calculated using it are estimates, not final.
  • The final answer key will be released after review of all valid objections received during the window.
  • The official result will be based on the final answer key, not the provisional one.
  • Use only official RRB regional websites or the authorized login portal to access the answer key — avoid unofficial third-party links for login.
  • Keep your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password handy before attempting to log in.

RRB Group D City Intimation Slip and Admit Card 2026

  • The first City Intimation Slip was released on 24th July 2026.
  • The E-Call Letter (Admit Card) becomes available approximately 4 days before the date mentioned in the City Intimation Slip.
  • The first Admit Card release is reported as 31st July 2026.
  • Since the CBT is being conducted in multiple phases through August 2026, City Intimation Slips and Admit Cards will continue to be released in batches closer to each phase's exam dates.

Aadhaar-Based Biometric Authentication: Important Instructions

The official notice places strong emphasis on Aadhaar verification for CEN 09/2025 candidates:

  • Aadhaar-linked biometric authentication is mandatory at the exam centre before entry into the exam hall.
  • Candidates must carry either their original Aadhaar card or a printout of e-verified Aadhaar.
  • Candidates who have not completed Aadhaar verification are advised to do so in advance by logging into the official portal with their registered credentials.
  • Even candidates who verified Aadhaar during the application stage must ensure their Aadhaar status is "unlocked" in the UIDAI system before arriving at the centre. A locked Aadhaar can cause avoidable delays during registration on exam day.
  • Candidates are advised to check their Aadhaar lock/unlock status on the official UIDAI portal a few days before the exam.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB region (linked via rrbapply.gov.in).

  3. Log in using your registration number and date of birth or password.
  4. Download and take a printout of the City Intimation Slip and, later, the Admit Card.
  5. Verify your Aadhaar unlock status on the UIDAI portal before the exam date.

RRB Group D 2026: What Candidates Should Do Next

  • Revise core subjects: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Science, and General Awareness on Current Affairs.
  • Practice previous years' RRB Group D papers and full-length mock tests.
  • Keep login credentials for rrbapply.gov.in ready for Aadhaar verification and e-call letter download.

RRB Group D Physical Exam Date 2026 has been released zone-wise by the respective Railway Recruitment Cells (RRCs) for candidates shortlisted in the CBT under CEN No. 08/2024. The Physical Efficiency Test (PET) is being conducted from 25th July 2026 to 11th September 2026, with dates varying by zone. As of 30th July 2026, PET schedules have been announced for Ajmer, Chennai, Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bilaspur, Chandigarh, Ranchi, Kolkata, and Mumbai zones, while some zones (including Patna and Hubballi) have been postponed and several others are yet to release their schedule. This article covers the complete zone-wise PET dates, PET criteria, admit card details, and required documents.

RRB Group D PET 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Recruitment Body Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)
Recruitment Notice CEN No. 08/2024
Post Level-1 (Group D) Posts
Exam Stage Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
CBT Result Declared 1st July 2026
Total Vacancies (CEN 08/2024) 32,438
PET Nature Qualifying only; no marks added to final merit list
Selection Process CBT → PET → Document Verification → Medical Examination
PET Period (All Zones Combined) 25th July 2026 to 11th September 2026 (zone-wise)

RRB Group D PET Dates 2026: Zone-Wise Schedule

The table below lists the current status of the RRB Group D PET schedule for every RRB/RRC zone. Dates marked "Not Yet Announced" have not been released by the concerned RRC as of 30th July 2026.

RRB/RRC Zone PET Dates 2026 Status
Ajmer (North Western Railway) 29 July - 1 August 2026 Ongoing; 1 August reserved for candidates unable to attend earlier dates
Prayagraj (North Central Railway) 25 - 28 July 2026 Completed; result already declared
Chennai (Southern Railway) 29 - 31 July 2026 Ongoing
Patna (East Central Railway) Originally 28 - 29 July 2026 Postponed; revised date Not Yet Announced
Hubballi / Bengaluru (South Western Railway) Originally 30 - 31 July 2026 Postponed until further notice
Bilaspur (South East Central Railway) From 2 August 2026 onwards Scheduled
Chandigarh (Northern Railway) From 24 August 2026 onwards Scheduled
Bhopal (West Central Railway) 31 August - 3 September 2026 Scheduled; to be held at Jabalpur
Mumbai (Central Railway & Western Railway) 1 - 5 September 2026 Scheduled; to be held at Nagpur
Ranchi (South Eastern Railway) 9 - 11 September 2026 Tentative
Kolkata (Eastern Railway & South Eastern Railway) September 2026 (exact dates awaited) Tentative

RRB Group D Ajmer PET Exam Date 2026

The Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC), Jaipur has scheduled the PET for candidates shortlisted under CEN No. 08/2024 from 29 July to 31 July 2026, with 1 August 2026 kept as a final opportunity for candidates unable to appear earlier for valid reasons. The test is being held at G.L.O. Ground, A.D.S.A. Stadium, near DRM Office, Mall Road, Ajmer. Male candidates must report at 6:00 AM, and female/transgender candidates at 9:00 AM on the final PET day. Candidates must carry their e-call letter, original photo ID, and original Aadhaar card candidates without these documents will not be permitted to appear.

RRB Group D Prayagraj PET Exam Date 2026

The RRB Group D Prayagraj PET was conducted from 25 to 28 July 2026 at DSA Ground, near Prayagraj Railway Station. The RRC, North Central Railway has already declared the PET result, with 251 candidates qualifying for the next stage Document Verification and Medical Examination.

RRB Group D Chennai PET Exam Date 2026

The Southern Railway zone's PET is scheduled from 29 to 31 July 2026. Candidates should download their e-call letter from the official RRC Chennai website and carry the required identity documents to the venue.

RRB Group D Patna PET Exam Date 2026 (Postponed)

The PET originally scheduled for 28-29 July 2026 under RRC, East Central Railway (Patna) has been postponed due to administrative reasons. Free travel passes issued earlier to eligible SC/ST candidates for the postponed dates have also been cancelled. The revised date is Not Yet Announced; candidates should keep checking the official RRC Patna website.

RRB Group D Hubballi (Bengaluru) PET Exam Date 2026 (Postponed)

The South Western Railway zone's PET, originally set for 30-31 July 2026, has been postponed until further notice. The revised schedule will be published on the official RRC Hubballi website.

RRB Group D Bilaspur, Chandigarh, Bhopal, Mumbai, Ranchi and Kolkata PET Dates 2026

Zone PET Date Venue
Bilaspur (South East Central Railway) From 2 August 2026 onwards Not Yet Announced
Chandigarh (Northern Railway) From 24 August 2026 onwards Not Yet Announced
Bhopal (West Central Railway) 31 August - 3 September 2026 Jabalpur (four-day test)
Mumbai (Central Railway & Western Railway) 1 - 5 September 2026 Rail Stadium, Central Railway Colony, Ajni, Nagpur
Ranchi (South Eastern Railway) 9 - 11 September 2026 (tentative) Not Yet Announced
Kolkata (Eastern Railway & South Eastern Railway) September 2026 (tentative) Not Yet Announced

RRB Group D PET Criteria 2026

The PET is qualifying in nature and must be completed successfully in a single attempt. Candidates who fail the first component are not permitted to attempt the second.

Category Requirement
Male Candidates Lift and carry 35 kg for 100 metres within 2 minutes, in a single chance, without dropping the weight
Run 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds, in a single chance
Female Candidates Lift and carry 20 kg for 100 metres within 2 minutes, in a single chance, without dropping the weight
Run 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds, in a single chance

Documents Required for RRB Group D PET 2026

  • PET e-call letter (printed copy)
  • Original photo ID proof
  • Original Aadhaar card
  • Any additional document specified in the zone-specific e-call letter

Document requirements may vary slightly by zone. Candidates should always check the instructions listed on their own e-call letter before travelling to the venue.

How to Download RRB Group D PET Admit Card 2026

  1. Visit the official website of the concerned RRC/RRB zone (e.g., rrcjaipur.in, rrb.digialm.com, rrchubli.in check the zone applicable to you).
  2. Look for the "RRB Group D PET Admit Card / e-Call Letter CEN 08/2024" link.
  3. Log in using your registration number and date of birth or password.
  4. Download and take a printout of the e-call letter.
  5. Carry the printed admit card along with the required documents to the PET venue.

The e-call letter is also sent via SMS and email to the registered mobile number and email ID of shortlisted candidates.

RRB Group D PET 2026: Important Instructions

  • Only candidates provisionally shortlisted after the CBT are eligible to appear for the PET.
  • Report to the venue at the reporting time mentioned on the e-call letter; late entry may not be permitted.
  • Both PET components (lift-and-carry and running) must be completed in a single attempt.
  • Candidates without a valid e-call letter and original ID/Aadhaar will not be allowed to appear.
  • PET is qualifying only; no marks are added to the final merit list.
  • Candidates found attempting to influence the RRC may have their candidature cancelled, and legal action may follow.
  • Keep checking the official RRC website of your zone regularly for venue, reporting time, and any date revisions.

How to Raise Objection Claim-Objection on PSLA26 Answer Key

CG Vyapam accepts objections only through the online portal. Postal submissions and in-person objections will not be accepted. Steps to raise an objection:

  1. Go to the official CG Vyapam website: vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in
  2. Log in to your candidate profile using your registered mobile number and password.
  3. Navigate to the Claim-Objection (दावा-आपत्ति) tab.
  4. Select the question(s) you wish to object to and enter your claim as per the instructions given.
  5. Pay the objection fee of Rs. 50 per question. The objection process is incomplete without fee payment.
  6. Upload soft copies of supporting documents/proof for your claim.
  7. Submit the objection and download the acknowledgement receipt after successful submission.

A detailed step-by-step manual for the objection process is available directly on the VYAPAM portal, and candidates are advised to read it carefully before proceeding.

How to Raise an Objection Against the Answer Key

  3. Attach a copy of an authentic source document or proof supporting your objection.
  4. Pay the non-refundable objection fee of ₹50/- per objection through the online payment mode.
  5. Submit the objection before the closing time and retain the confirmation for your records.

  • Objections submitted without payment of the prescribed fee will not be entertained.
  • Objections received after 06.08.2026, 12:00 p.m. will not be entertained.
  • Objections submitted through any mode other than the one prescribed in the official notice will not be entertained.
  • Any objection that does not meet the above conditions will be rejected automatically without assigning any reason.
  • No representation regarding any question or the provisional Model Answer will be entertained after the closing date for objections.
  • If no objection is received for a question, the provisional Model Answer Key will be deemed final for that question.
  • The decision of the High Court of Judicature at Patna on all objections is final, and no further correspondence will be entertained.
  • Candidates are advised to keep visiting the official website regularly for further updates.

What Happens After the Objection Window Closes?

The provisional Model Answer Key will be finalised after the High Court reviews all valid objections received within the window. This finalised key will then be used as the official Model Answer for generating the result of the Computer Operator-cum-Typist Recruitment Examination, 2026. Candidates should note that vacancy details, post-wise qualification, selection process, and salary information are Not Available Officially in this particular notice, as it deals only with the answer key and objection process.

Visit the official CGPSC website to check the answer key, estimate your score, and complete the objection process within the deadline.

Download CGPSC Assistant Librarian Model Answer Key 2026

How to Raise an Online Objection Against the Answer Key

Candidates can follow these steps to submit an objection through the CGPSC website:

  1. Visit the official CGPSC website and log in to the candidate dashboard.
  2. Go to the Activity Section and click on Objection Filing.
  3. On the new page, select the exam name, question paper, set, and the question number you want to object to.
  4. Select the applicable type of objection (see list below).
  5. Clearly write the reason for the objection in the box provided.
  6. Upload supporting proof as a PDF document (maximum size 1MB per question). Proof must include the source name, author, edition/publication date, and reference page number — mere links or website names without this detail will not be accepted.
  7. Use the Add button to submit multiple objections; unwanted entries can be removed before final submission.
  8. Click Save after entering all objections.
  9. Proceed to the fee payment page and click Pay Now to pay Rs. 50 per question for all objections raised.
  10. After successful payment, download the acknowledgement/receipt from the Dashboard under Activity Section > Download Acknowledgement.

Types of Objections Accepted

Objection Type Description
All Answer Options Incorrect All given options for a question are wrong
Commission's Answer Option Incorrect The answer option released by the commission is wrong
More Than One Correct Option More than one answer option is correct
Question is Wrong The question itself is incorrect
Question Out of Syllabus The question is not part of the prescribed syllabus
Hindi-English Translation Mismatch There is a factual difference between the Hindi and English translation of the question

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Objections can be submitted only through the online mode; no offline application or document will be accepted at the commission office.
  • Candidates get only one opportunity to submit all objections together; once the fee is paid, the process is considered complete and objections cannot be filed again.
  • Candidates are responsible for avoiding phishing, hacking, or other cyber risks during online banking/payment.
  • If the fee payment is unsuccessful, if entries are made in different sets of the same question paper, or if the prescribed process is not followed correctly, the submitted objection will be automatically rejected, and no request/appeal regarding this will be entertained by the commission.

Every paper carries 100 questions. The table below summarizes how many questions were deleted in the final key for each subject, based on the officially released PDFs.
